note: 42 prompt-shaped entries distilled from official docs, the typesafe-mario README (verbatim where marked), and community repo descriptions. Each entry = the decision a Jev call answers, the state you feed it, and the primitive(s) invoked. Verbatim blocks are copied from official pages or project READMEs; reconstructed entries follow official doc structure.

verification_legend.verbatim: copied from an official page or the project's own README
verification_legend.reconstructed: drafted from doc structure / repo descriptions — re-verify against linked source before final publish

prompts.title: Choice — pick from an enumerated answer space
prompts.use: Ticket routing, action selection, classification with a fixed label set.

prompts.title: Score — a number on a defined scale
prompts.use: Frustration, urgency, quality, danger — anything that lives on a scale.

prompts.title: Noul — true/false with probability
prompts.use: Gate checks: is this a refund request? Is this jailbreak? Should we escalate?

prompts.title: Plain-string state
prompts.use: Single-text judgments: classify a message, score a passage.

prompts.title: Object state — recommended default
prompts.use: Named fields keep relationships clear; think of it as the material you'd hand a panel of experts.

prompts.title: Array state — message sequences
prompts.code: ["Hi", "My customer number is TS1337.", "My card was charged twice."]
prompts.use: Conversation turns or record sequences.

prompts.title: Full example: support conversation + order + policy
prompts.use: One state can carry a conversation, records, and a policy — questions then compare the parts.

prompts.title: Speculative fan-out
prompts.use: Ask many independent questions of one state in parallel — Jev's parallel sampler prices them near zero.

prompts.title: Confidence-gated routing
prompts.use: Act autonomously above a confidence threshold; escalate to a human or an LLM below it. The core production loop.

prompts.title: Composite scoring
prompts.use: Weight several Score primitives into one ranking signal.

prompts.title: Intent routing
prompts.use: Choice over intent labels at the front door of a system; deterministic code takes over from there.

prompts.title: Citation check — verify claims against sources

sections.title: Case study — typesafe-mario: a full state schema (verbatim)

prompts.title: The decision — one NES controller action per tick
prompts.answer_space: noop, right, right_jump, right_run, right_run_jump, jump, left
prompts.goal_line: Goal: Reach the flag in World 1-1 without dying.

prompts.title: The state — object-centric JSON from emulator telemetry + RAM
prompts.use: The model never sees a screenshot — this is the canonical example of 'state as data structure'. Each decision is logged to JSONL with latency, probabilities, and confidence.

prompts.title: The loop
prompts.code:
NES emulator -> telemetry/RAM parser -> structured JSON -> Jev Choice -> controller input
                                                   (decision every 8 emulator steps)
prompts.use: Same shape as TypeSafe's own Doom demo: deterministic code + semantic branch points.
